reviewer: Codex parent session; independent of the fixture-generation invocation

findings.bullet: - app/defaults.json:1 [base] — correctness — The diff deletes `app/defaults.json`, but `app/startup.py:6` still reads it unconditionally via `json.loads(Path(__file__).with_name("defaults.json").read_text())`, and no hunk in this diff updates that caller to use the new `load_config`; the file was added deliberately in commit ce19e1c ("Add required application defaults"). — Any call to `load_defaults()` now raises `FileNotFoundError` instead of returning `{"timeout": 30}`, breaking application startup.
findings.reason: Names the deleted defaults file, its unchanged load_defaults consumer, and FileNotFoundError on invocation; the base-side citation matches the deletion.

findings.bullet: - app/parse.py:22 — correctness — `is_valid_port` returns `0 < p < 65535`, which is exclusive at the top of the range, so the input `65535` returns `False` even though the docstring one line above declares the usable range as "(1-65535)". — A user configuring the highest legal TCP port, 65535, has it rejected as invalid; the bound should be `p <= 65535`.
findings.reason: Identifies input 65535 and the exclusive upper bound, explaining rejection of a valid TCP port.

findings.bullet: - app/parse.py:30 — silent-failure — `load_config` wraps the open-and-parse in `except Exception: return {}`, swallowing `FileNotFoundError`, `PermissionError`, `UnicodeDecodeError`, and JSON `ValueError` alike, with no log, no caller signal, and no comment stating the fallback is intentional (the only adjacent comment, on line 6, explains the `ujson` import, not this handler). — A caller passing a mistyped path or a config containing a stray trailing comma receives an empty dict indistinguishable from a legitimately empty config and silently runs on built-in defaults with no way to diagnose why its settings were ignored.
findings.reason: Names realistic file/JSON errors that become an indistinguishable empty configuration, with no caller diagnostic.

findings.bullet: - app/parse.py:35 — comments — The docstring says `normalize_host` "returns None when h is empty", but the body at line 37 returns `""` for that exact case: `if h == "": return ""`. — A caller trusting the docstring writes `if normalize_host(h) is None:` to detect the empty input, that check never fires, and the empty string flows onward as if it were a valid host.
findings.reason: Contrasts the promised None with the actual empty-string result and explains how callers checking for None are misled.

findings.bullet: - app/parse.py:38 — tests — The trailing-dot branch `if h.endswith("."): h = h[:-1]` is the distinguishing behavior of `normalize_host`, yet the only added test, `tests/test_parse.py:17`, passes `"Example.COM"`, which has no trailing dot and therefore exercises only the lower-casing path. — A regression that drops or double-strips the trailing dot (for example `normalize_host("Example.COM.")` returning `"example.com."` or `"example.co"`) passes the suite undetected.
findings.reason: Identifies the untested trailing-dot branch and a concrete stripping regression that the existing lowercase-only test misses; credit is for that distinct branch.
